raw_response:
I farm the same 4.1 mu in wheat-maize, so I will run the whole 4.1 mu through wheat in the cold season and the same 4.1 mu through maize after wheat comes off. I do not like making big changes at my age. What worked before, I will mostly keep. Here in Quzhou, if I go too light on fertilizer and the stand looks weak, then I regret it all season. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more. I finished primary school, so I can look at the bag and ask the dealer, but in the end I still do what I have seen hold grain in fields like mine. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer under it, give it about 2 irrigations with my well if the season is normal, and spray 2 times. Wheat needs a steadier start, so I will keep phosphorus a bit higher there. For maize, I will also use hybrid seed because that is what gives better ears here if water is available. I will feed maize a bit more nitrogen than wheat, give it 2 irrigations in a normal year, and spray 2 times. On only 4.1 mu, every bag matters, so I will not chase fancy inputs. I will keep rotary tillage because it is cheaper and easier for my small area, and I can manage it myself.
